title: Brihadisvara Temple, Thanjavur
description: Granite Hindu temple dedicated to Shiva located in Thanjavur, built by Chola emperor Rajaraja I between 1003 and 1010 CE; UNESCO World Heritage Site.

title: Konark Sun Temple
description: 13th-century CE Sun Temple at Konark attributed to King Narasimhadeva I of the Eastern Ganga dynasty, designed as a colossal 24-wheeled stone chariot.

title: Ajanta Caves
description: Approximately 30 rock-cut Buddhist cave monuments dating from the 2nd century BCE to about 480 CE, famous for masterpieces of Buddhist religious art and murals.

title: Hampi Monuments Complex
description: Ruins of the capital city of the historic Vijayanagara Empire on the banks of the Tungabhadra River, featuring Vitthala Temple stone chariot and Virupaksha shrine.

title: Rani ki Vav (The Queen's Stepwell)
description: Subterranean stepwell built during the Chaulukya dynasty, designed as an inverted temple highlighting the sanctity of water with over 500 principal sculptures.

title: Qutb Minar and Monuments Complex
description: Fluted red sandstone minaret of 72.5 meters height founded by Qutb-ud-din Aibak in 1192 CE, featuring the 4th-century Gupta iron pillar with no corrosion.

title: Khajuraho Group of Monuments
description: Nagara-style Hindu and Jain temples built between 950 and 1050 CE by the Chandela dynasty, celebrated for intricate relief friezes of everyday and celestial life.

title: Nalanda Mahavihara Archaeological Site
description: Monastic and scholastic university complex flourishing from the 5th to the 12th century CE under the Gupta and Pala empires.

title: Shore Temple, Mamallapuram
description: 8th-century structural temple built of cut granite blocks by the Pallava King Narasimhavarman II overlooking the Bay of Bengal.

title: Bhimbetka Rock Shelters
description: Paleolithic and Mesolithic rock art showing human figures, animal hunts, and geometric symbols spanning over 100,000 years of human habitational traces.

title: Dholavira: a Harappan City
description: Ancient Indus Valley Civilization urban center in Kutch with monumental water reservoirs, stepped stone channels, and citadel fortifications.

title: Martand Sun Temple
description: 8th-century stone temple dedicated to Surya built by King Lalitaditya Muktapida of the Karkota dynasty, blending Gandharan, Roman, and Kashmiri architectural styles.

title: Kangra Fort
description: Ancient fort built by the Katoch dynasty on the confluence of the Banganga and Manjhi rivers, one of the oldest dated forts in India.

title: Jageshwar Group of Temples
description: Cluster of over 100 stone shrines dating from the 7th to the 12th century CE situated within a sacred deodar forest in Almora.

title: Chittorgarh Fort
description: Sprawling hilltop fortress in Mewar featuring the 9-story Vijay Stambha (Tower of Victory) and ancient stepwells carved into basalt cliffs.

title: Golconda Fort and Qutb Shahi Tombs
description: Medieval fortified citadel renowned for its acoustic architecture where a clap under the entrance dome can be clearly heard at the highest point 1 km away.

title: Bekal Fort
description: Largest sea-facing laterite fort in Kerala built by Shivappa Nayaka of Keladi in 1650 CE, featuring a keyhole observation tower.

title: Bishnupur Terracotta Temples
description: 17th-century brick temples built by Malla kings featuring curved 'chala' roofs and thousands of intricately molded terracotta narrative panels.

title: Talatal Ghar and Rang Ghar, Ahom Kingdom
description: 18th-century brick palace and amphitheatre in Sivasagar constructed with special indigenous cement made of sticky rice, duck eggs, and fish oil.

title: Unakoti Rock-Cut Relief Sculptures
description: Ancient Shaivite pilgrimage spot nestled in forested hills with colossal vertical bas-relief carvings dating to the 8th–9th century CE.

title: Cellular Jail National Memorial
description: Colonial prison complex in Port Blair comprising seven radiating wings designed for solitary confinement, now an important national freedom struggle memorial.

title: Diu Fort
state: Dadra and Nagar Haveli and Daman and Diu
description: Historic sea-girt sandstone fortress on Diu Island constructed by the Portuguese in 1535 following a defence alliance with Sultan Bahadur Shah of Gujarat.

title: Arikamedu Archaeological Site
description: Ancient coastal port and bead-making emporium on the Ariyankuppam River active from the 2nd century BCE with extensive Roman trade artifacts (amphorae, terra sigillata).

title: Le Corbusier Capitol Complex
description: UNESCO World Heritage modern architectural complex featuring the Secretariat, High Court, and Palace of Assembly in monumental exposed raw concrete (beton brut).
